messages.content: Our plan integer-foundations has one current chapter lesson: AoPS V1-C05, Using the Integers. Its agreed objective is to use quotient-remainder representation to compute remainders and explain its consequences. We are at the independent check. I will give no hints or solutions during this check.
What is the remainder when 29 is divided by 7? Explain your calculation.
29 = 4 times 7 plus 1. Therefore the remainder is 1.
A different task: n has remainder 3 when divided by 7. What is the remainder of 2n+1? Explain why it works for every such integer n.

turns: Write n = 7k + 3 for an integer k. Then 2n + 1 = 14k + 7 = 7(2k + 1), so it is divisible by 7 and the remainder is 0. This works for every integer k.
